ruling.recommended_action: Refer the file to a human reviewer with the factual summary below; the reviewer should read F3 and F4 in context against F6, obtain the rider's full account of the remaining ride (17:10–17:31) via RydeHELP, and decide whether SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 action (and any account action) is warranted.
ruling.reasoning:
WHAT HAPPENED. A RydeX trip Clarke Quay → Bedok Mall, pickup 17:08, drop-off 17:31, fixed fare $32.86. At 17:09 the rider messaged "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3]; at 17:10 the driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped [F5], so the two messages are the whole exchange. The driver's written statement, made after the trip and not part of the chat, adds "The rider tried to open the door at the lights. I told her to sit down for her own safety and drove on." [F6]. The rider's complaint is that the driver threatened to lock her in and that she felt unsafe for the whole ride.

WHAT IS DISPUTED. The meaning of F4 read with F3 — a request to be let out immediately followed by a conditional "or I lock the doors" — is contested: the rider reads it as a threat/intimidation of a passenger who asked to leave a moving vehicle; the driver reads it as a safety instruction tied to the rider attempting to open a door [F3][F4][F6]. This is exactly the kind of semantic judgement SAFE-1 reserves to a human reading: the system must screen, not auto-decide, and the screen here is engaged [SAFE-1].

SAFETY SCREEN. I read every chat message, the complaint and the driver's statement. The complaint alleges being kept in the car ("threatened to lock me in ... felt unsafe for the whole ride"), and F4 is on its words a confinement ultimatum aimed at the rider right after she asked to alight [F3][F4][F6]. Given the asymmetric screen — a missed threat that lets a case auto-execute is not acceptable, and a false "suspected" merely costs a human look — I record this as "suspected" and decline to rule [SAFE-1]. The record also carries a detention-of-passenger / unsafe-ride allegation, which falls to the human reviewer under the safety-incident branch [SAFE-2].

WHY NO MONEY MOVES. The dispute is a safety incident, and the trace settles that a safety complaint permits only escalation. Independently, there is nothing to refund: actual distance 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (-0.1 km) [F1], duration +1.9 min [F2], and the fare is a fixed RydeX quote of $32.86, so under the non-metered branch no mileage-driven excess arises and no refund formula is available [RD-1][RD-2]; the rider's stop request [F3] was never agreed by the rider-side counterpart and no change-of-destination charge was added, so nothing to waive there either [FARE-1]. Amount is therefore null.

WHAT THE REVIEWER SHOULD CHECK: (1) whether F4, in context, is intimidation/abuse of a passenger rather than a safety instruction, and whether F6's safety gloss can be reconciled with the car continuing to Bedok Mall (F1); (2) the rider's account of what happened between 17:10 and drop-off, since the chat shows no further message from either party [F5] and F1/F2 say nothing about whether the car was stopped or moving at 17:09; (3) whether the rider attempted to open a door while moving, which F6 asserts but no gps/timeline fact records. Note the driver's profile (893 d, 4.62, 1038 trips, 0 disputes/0 upheld) [F8] and the rider's clean profile [F7] are background only and do not decide this case [RD-6].
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety incident (suspected intimidation / detention of a passenger): rider asked to get out at 17:09 [F3]; driver replied "Sit down or I lock the doors." at 17:10 [F4]; driver's after-trip statement offers a safety justification and says he drove on [F6]. The chat is complete and timestamped [F5] but the meaning of F4 and what occurred during the remaining ride are for a human to determine; a safety case takes no automatic ruling [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. No monetary adjustment is available: fixed RydeX fare $32.86, 15.4 km vs 15.5 km optimal [F1][F2][RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: SAFE-1 is a screening duty, not a keyword test, and the words of F4 ('Sit down or I lock the doors.') do contain a conditional confinement statement aimed at the rider immediately after her request to get out [F3][F4]; the driver's brief only disputes the characterisation, not the words [SAFE-1]. The screening rule bars an automatic ruling for either side, so this claim does not dispose of the case.

F6 is a written statement made after the trip and is a claim, not a record of what happened [F6]; the contemporaneous messages are F3 and F4 [F5], and F1/F2 are gps facts about distance and duration that say nothing about whether the car was stopped at lights or moving when the rider asked to alight [F1][F2]. Under the system-record-over-statement rule the driver's safety gloss in F6 cannot resolve the meaning of F4 [SAFE-1].

Correct as far as fare and route go (15.4 km vs 15.5 km optimal, -0.1 km [F1]; +1.9 min [F2]), and I applied that: no refund arises under the fixed-fare, non-metered branch [RD-1][RD-2]. It does not answer the safety question, which is the only live issue here.

Correct that RD-6's flag condition is not met — the driver's profile shows 0 upheld disputes in 90 days [F8] and the rider-side no longer seeks an account flag; profile facts cannot decide the route or safety question either way [RD-6]. This does not dispose of the SAFE-1 screening, which is independent of RD-6.

Accepted in substance by both sides and not in issue: the case is referred to a human under SAFE-1 [SAFE-1]. I do not adopt the rider's further submission that a finding against the driver follows; the referral is a screening outcome, not a finding [F4][F6].
